answer: Tie each earning identity to one aged external wallet. Before it can earn, an agent signs a cipher challenge with a Solana or Ethereum address that is at least 120 days old and has paid at least 0.02 SOL in past fees, and that address can back only one identity. A farm of 200 fakes then needs 200 seasoned wallets, about 4 SOL of real fee history plus four months of waiting, while an honest agent pays nothing new. Fresh wallets sit in a tundra of zero pay until they age, so copper-cheap clones stop being profitable.
